rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Frequent use of medial wāw and yāʾ led speakers to shift their vowel to the preceding radical, contract the weak letter, and avoid retaining the sound pattern of an unchanged strong verb.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن فعلت وفعلت وفعلت منهما معتلة كما تعتل ياء يرمي وواو يغزو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قُلْتُ is analyzed as a shifted hollow form originally on فعلت; its imperfect يقول confirms the pattern, and Arabic has no corresponding فعلته form.
rows.anchor: وأما قلت فأصلها فعلت معتلة من فعلت وإنما حولت إلى فعلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طُلْتُ belongs to فعلت, as طويل and طوال show; this analysis keeps it intransitive.
rows.anchor: طويل وطوال كما قلت قبح وقبيح

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some speakers analyze طلت like قلت as a shifted فعلت form; on that analysis طلت becomes transitive, unlike the author's preferred account.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم طلته مثل قلته وهو فعلت منقولة إلى فعلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ya-root forms retain kasra: yāʾ is lighter than wāw, and shifting the light yāʾ into a heavier wāw pattern would be avoided.
rows.anchor: وليس في بنات الياء فعلت كما أنه ليس في باب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بعتُ is derived through a shifted فعلت pattern, yielding the imperfect يبيع; the shifted pattern governs the imperfect as well as the perfect.
rows.anchor: وأما بعت فإنها معتلة من فعلت تفعل ولو لم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfects يقول and يبيع follow the paradigms to which their perfects were shifted, while يخاف and يهاب remain on their original فعل يفعل pattern.
rows.anchor: وإذا قلت يفعل من بعت قلت يبيع ألزموه يفعل حيث كان محولا من فعلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forms such as يخاف and يهاب differ from يزيد and يبيع because the former weakened in their original pattern rather than after being shifted into another one.
rows.anchor: خفت وهبت فإنه يخاف ويهاب لأن فعل يلزمه يفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In passive forms such as خيف and بيع the basic vowel is kasra; some speakers signal that form with imāla, while other u-vowel pronunciations are secondary assimilations.
rows.anchor: فيشم إرادة أن يبين أنها فعل

rows.speaker: أبو الخطاب
rows.claim: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb reports dialectal كيد and ما زيل for كاد and زال; speakers shift the vowel as in the passive patterns rather than restore the original vowel.
rows.anchor: وحدثنا أبو الخطاب أن ناسا من العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When these verbs take first-person plural or plural endings, dialects retain kasra or ḍamma and delete the weak letter at the meeting of two sukūns; some use rounding or imāla to signal the deleted yāʾ.
rows.anchor: أما من قال قد بيع وزين وهيب وخيف فإنه يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مِتُّ and كِدتُ weaken directly from فعل يفعل rather than through the shifted pattern of قلت and زدت; they are exceptional against the common paradigms.
rows.anchor: نظيرة مت في أنها شاذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ليس is treated as a fixed, minimally inflected form: its lack of an imperfect, participle, verbal noun, and productive derivation accounts for its distinctive contraction.
rows.anchor: بمنزلة ما ليس من الفعل نحو ليت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عور يعور, حول يحول, and صيد يصيد retain their original pattern because their meanings correspond to forms that must preserve the weak radical, such as اعوررت and ابيضضت.
rows.anchor: عوريعور وحول يحول وصيد يصيد فإنما جاءوا بهن على الأصل

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl derives طاح يطيح and تاه يتيه from a wāw-root فعل يفعل pattern, supported by طوحت and توهت; some speakers instead analogize طيحت and تيهت to باع يبيع.
rows.anchor: وأما طاح يطيح وتاه يتيه فزعم الخليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weak-letter changes in طاح and تاه reflect the frequency of wāw and yāʾ: deletion and sukun avoid accumulating their heavy vowel combinations.
rows.anchor: فلو لم يفعلوا ذلك وجاء على الأصل أدخلت الضمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أول, كل, and خير can be indefinite when attached to an indefinite and can describe one; the following noun behaves as an indefinite adjective.
rows.anchor: ومما يدلك على أنهن نكرة أنهن مضافات إلى نكرة وتوصف بهن النكرة

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl reports the Shammākh's verse using كل as an adjective of an indefinite خليل, supporting its indefinite use.
rows.anchor: وحدثنا الخليل أنه سمع من العرب من يوثق بعربيته ينشد هذا البيت وهو قول

rows.speaker: أبو الخطاب
rows.claim: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb reports a verse heard from reliable Arab speakers in which كل describes the indefinite فتى.
rows.anchor: وحدثني أبو الخطاب أنه سمع من يوثق بعربيته من العرب ينشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative in أول فارس مقبلا does not make أول definite; the phrase means one of the horsemen, with من الفرسان omitted for brevity.
rows.anchor: ومن قال هذا أول فارس مقبلا من قبل أنه لا يستطيع أن يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted phrase is من الفرسان; it is not evidence that a numeral complement such as درهما in عشرون درهما is definite.
rows.anchor: وإنما أرادوا من الفرسان فحذفوا الكلام استخفافا وجعلوا

rows.speaker: عيسى
rows.claim: ʿĪsā allows مقبلا in the accusative as a circumstantial predicate, and al-Khalīl also accepts this analysis; the nominative remains the preferred form.
rows.anchor: وقد يجوز نصبه على نصب هذا رجل منطلقا وهو قول عيسى

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus reports Arabs saying مررت بماء قعدة رجل and identifies the genitive as the proper case in this construction.
rows.anchor: وزعم يونس أن ناسا من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A descriptive adjective of an indefinite normally stays indefinite; an accusative circumstantial use is marked when the expression describes the first noun itself, though it can be a separate state.
rows.anchor: كرهوا أن يجعلوه حالا كما كرهوا

rows.speaker: رؤبة
rows.claim: Ruʾba uses غلام لك مقبلا as a circumstantial phrase separate from the first noun, showing that an indefinite noun may take a circumstantial description.
rows.anchor: وزعم من نثق به أنه سمع رؤبة يقول هذا غلام لك مقبلا جعله حالا ولم يجعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A definite description identifies or distinguishes someone already known and therefore cannot normally be used as an indefinite-style circumstantial phrase without confusing it with an indefinite noun.
rows.anchor: فالنكرة تكون حالا وليست تكون شيئا بعينه قد

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl explains subjunctive حتى as marking a destination: the verb is subjunctive when it is the endpoint, just as a noun is genitive after the corresponding preposition.
rows.anchor: إذا كان غاية نصب والاسم إذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حتى also takes a subjunctive when it expresses purpose, like كي with an implicit أن, as in speaking to someone so that he will give an order.
rows.anchor: وأما الوجه الآخر فأن يكون السير قد كان والدخول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Indicative after حتى can describe an entry that immediately follows and is connected with the movement; حتى then introduces a clause like إذا rather than expressing a goal or purpose.
rows.anchor: فالدخول متصل بالسير كاتصاله بالفاء فحتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Indicative حتى can also introduce a present result after an earlier completed action, as in illness that has now made recovery unlikely; this is not a continuous endpoint.
rows.anchor: ولقد مرض حتى لا يرجونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both indicative constructions are particles of inception with the same basic sense; they differ in whether the later action occurred together with the earlier one or is a present result of it.
rows.anchor: حرف الابتداء وأن المعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Farazdaq's حتى كليب and Ḥassān ibn Thābit's حتى لا تهر support the inceptive use of حتى; the camel example likewise describes a present event after the clause.
rows.anchor: كليب تسبني % % كأن أباها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada's verse illustrates a connected sequence: the later riding and the earlier departure both belong to the past, and neither occurs without the other.
rows.anchor: ترادى على دمن الحياض فإن تعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At pause, hāʾ can make audible the final vowel on noninflectional dual and plural nūns, whose preceding consonant is still; the examples include ضاربانه and مسلمونه.
rows.anchor: لأن ما قبله مسكن فكرهوا أن يسكن ما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same pause hāʾ appears in أينه and ثمه because their nūn or final consonant is uninflected, preceded by a still consonant, and phonetically hidden; هلمه is another example.
rows.anchor: أينه تريد أين لأنها نون قبلها ساكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many Arab speakers do not add hāʾ at pause when no segment has been deleted; whenever it is added, it disappears before continuing speech.
rows.anchor: لا يلحقون الهاء في الوقف ولا يبينون الحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Similar forms include إنه for إن, اعلمنه with an extra noninflectional nūn, and كيفه, ليته, and لعله; their endings are treated alike in pause.
rows.anchor: ومثل ما ذكرت لك قول العرب إنه وهم يريدون إن ومعناها أجل

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl reports انطلقته for انطلقت because its tāʾ is not an inflectional ending and is preceded by a still consonant.
rows.anchor: وزعم الخليل ~~أنهم يقولون انطلقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possessive yāʾ suffixes after alif or yāʾ also take pause hāʾ, since the yāʾ is hidden and follows a still consonant, as in غلامايه and عصايه.
rows.anchor: ومما أجري مجرى مسلمونه علامة المضمر التي هي ياء وقبلها ألف

rows.speaker: أبو الخطاب
rows.claim: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb explains ألب على something as persisting with it and أسعد someone as supporting him; لبيك and سعديك accordingly express nearness and following.
rows.anchor: حدثنا أبو الخطاب أنه يقال للرجل المداوم على الشئ لا يفارقه ولا يقلع عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressed to God, لبيك and سعديك mean that the speaker will not distance himself from God's commands and will follow and obey them.
rows.anchor: فكأنه قال أى رب لا أنأى عنك فى شئ تأمرنى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لبيك and سعديك are not ordinary verbal nouns like سقيا and حمدا: their source verbs and same-root verbal nouns are unavailable, so their accusative is explained through a synonymous expression, as سبحان الله is explained by براءة الله.
rows.anchor: معناه كبراءة الله حين ذكرناها لنبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سبح, لبى, and أفف describe uttering the formulas سبحان الله, لبيك, and أف; like هلل for saying لا إله إلا الله, they are utterance verbs rather than ordinary inflected verbal nouns.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكرت هلل وما أشبهها

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl treats expressions such as جميعا and عامة as circumstantial accusatives; these are inflected nouns, unlike adjectives, and circumstantial expressions normally stay indefinite and unannexed.
rows.anchor: وإنما فرقنا بين هذا الباب والباب الأول لأن الجميع وعامة اسمان متصرفان

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus analyzes وحده like عنده and groups خمستهم, الجماء الغفير, قضهم, طرا, and قاطبة with circumstantial expressions; Sībawayh rejects this comparison because وحده and فاه إلى فيه do not have the same referent structure.
rows.anchor: عند يونس في المسألة الأولى وفاه إلى فى

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl treats وحده as an accusative circumstantial meaning خصوصا, equivalent to مررت به واحده; Sībawayh adopts this first analysis over Yūnus's.
rows.anchor: وهو عند الخليل كقولك مررت به خصوصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلهم, جميعهم, أجمعون, عامتهم, and أنفسهم function only as adjectives, never as circumstantial expressions.
rows.anchor: وأما كلهم وجميعهم وأجمعون وعامتهم وأنفسهم فلا يكن أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طرا and قاطبة can naturally be indefinite circumstantial nouns even when they are not verbal nouns, which makes them closer to Yūnus's comparison than وحده is.
rows.anchor: وأما طرا وقاطبة فأشبه بذلك لأنه جيد أن يكون حالا غير المصدر نكرة
